title: Design and psychometric properties of the Persian knowledge, attitude, and practice about microplastics in human health (MIKAP) questionnaire among Iranian women
content:
by Zahra Seifi, Fatemeh Zarei, Fazlollah Ahmadi

Introduction

Given the growing concern over the impact of microplastics (MPs) on both environmental and human health, there is a critical need for tools to effectively assess public behavior regarding MPs. This study aimed to design and psychometrically validate a tool to assess the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice (KAP) of women regarding MPs. Women were specifically selected as the target population due to their primary roles in household management, food preparation, and higher usage of personal care products, which are key pathways for microplastic exposure.

Method

The instrument was developed using a deductive approach, and the psychometric properties of the MIKAP questionnaire were evaluated in terms of validity and reliability. An initial pool of 61 items was generated, which was subsequently reduced through rigorous validity assessment phases to a final 43-item version. Data were collected from two groups of 244 and 310 women aged 18 and above, who were selected for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), respectively.

Results

The MIKAP questionnaire consisted of 43 items across three domains defined a priori by the Knowledge–Attitude–Practice (KAP) theoretical framework; the nine factors identified by exploratory factor analysis were nested within these domains based on item loadings. Most items demonstrated acceptable quantitative face validity (impact score >1.5); two conceptually important items with lower impact scores were retained based on their theoretical relevance. Item-level CVR values ranged from 0.60 to 1.00. One item fell marginally below the predefined threshold of 0.62 and was retained after revision because of its conceptual relevance. I-CVI ranged from 0.8 to 1; S-CVI = 0.92; and Kappa ranged from 0.79 to 1, with an average of 0.92. The application of exploratory factor analysis to the data was significant (χ² = 4363.096; df = 903; p < 0.001). Confirmatory factor analysis of the three-domain MIKAP model resulted in the following fit indices: χ²/df: 1.536; p < 0.001; GFI: 0.84; CFI: 0.87 (modest values, below more stringent conventional cut-offs, and interpreted cautiously given the model's complexity and large degrees of freedom); RMSEA: 0.042; AGFI: 0.82; PGFI: 0.74; PNFI: 0.64; PCFI: 0.80, indicating acceptable, although not uniformly strong, overall model fit. Internal consistency estimates were acceptable to high at the domain level with a total Cronbach’s alpha of 0.920 and ICC = 0.846 (95% CI: 0.742–0.910).

Conclusion

The findings provide evidence supporting the validity and reliability of the MIKAP questionnaire for assessing the three constructs of knowledge, attitude, and practice regarding microplastics and health. This instrument can serve as a practical tool for health policymakers and environmental educators to design targeted interventions for reducing microplastic exposure.Clinical trial number: IRCT20240529061941N1 Registration Date 2024-07-12, 1403/04/22
